microtheory.name: literature
microtheory.definition: Literature + literary theory. Genres (epic, lyric, drama, novel, short story, essay). Literary devices (metaphor, irony, narrative voice, focalization). Major traditions: classical, medieval, Renaissance, Romantic, modernist, postmodernist. Theory: New Criticism, structuralism, deconstruction, reader-response, postcolonial, feminist, ecocritical. Substrate analogue: the discipline of meaning-making through written language.

concepts.name: narrative
concepts.definition: Sequence of related events constituting a story. Fabula (raw events) vs syuzhet (arrangement). Substrate analogue: substrate's structured event sequence.

concepts.name: fiction
concepts.definition: Imaginative literary work not literally true. Novel, short story, drama. Coleridge's willing suspension of disbelief.

concepts.name: poetry
concepts.definition: Language using metrical + sonic patterns for aesthetic + emotional + intellectual effect. Verse vs prose. Lyric, narrative, dramatic.

concepts.name: prose
concepts.definition: Ordinary writing not in metrical lines. Novel, essay, journalism.

concepts.name: epic
concepts.definition: Long narrative poem of heroic deeds. Iliad, Odyssey, Aeneid, Mahabharata, Beowulf.

concepts.name: lyric_poetry
concepts.definition: Short personal expression, often musical. Sappho, Horace, Petrarch.

concepts.name: novel
concepts.definition: Extended fictional prose narrative. Don Quixote 1605 often credited as first. Many forms: bildungsroman, picaresque, epistolary, stream of consciousness.

concepts.name: short_story
concepts.definition: Compressed prose fiction. Poe, Chekhov, Borges, Munro.

concepts.name: essay
concepts.definition: Montaigne 1580. Personal reflective prose. Familiar (Lamb) + formal (Bacon) traditions.

concepts.name: metaphor
concepts.definition: Implicit comparison. 'All the world's a stage'. Lakoff: conceptual not just rhetorical. Substrate analogue: substrate's cross-domain mapping.

concepts.name: simile
concepts.definition: Explicit comparison with 'like' or 'as'.

concepts.name: irony
concepts.definition: Discrepancy between literal + intended meaning. Verbal, situational, dramatic. Socratic irony.

concepts.name: symbolism
concepts.definition: Object/image carrying meaning beyond literal. Cross, dove, color.

concepts.name: narrator
concepts.definition: Voice telling story. First-person, third-person limited, omniscient, unreliable (Booth).

concepts.name: focalization_genette
concepts.definition: Gérard Genette. Whose perspective the narrative reflects. Internal vs external, fixed vs variable.

concepts.name: stream_of_consciousness
concepts.definition: Joyce, Woolf, Faulkner. Continuous interior monologue. Modernist innovation.

concepts.name: aristotelian_poetics_literary
concepts.definition: Aristotle ~335 BCE. Tragedy elements: plot, character, thought, diction, melody, spectacle. Foundation of Western literary theory.

concepts.name: new_criticism
concepts.definition: Brooks, Ransom, Wimsatt+Beardsley. Close reading of text as autonomous artifact. Intentional + affective fallacies. Mid-20th-c US dominant.

concepts.name: structuralism_literary
concepts.definition: Saussure → Barthes → Genette. Literature as system of differences + codes. Narratology.

concepts.name: deconstruction
concepts.definition: Derrida. Texts undermine their own apparent meanings via internal contradictions. Différance, supplement, trace.

concepts.name: reader_response
concepts.definition: Iser, Jauss, Fish. Meaning produced in encounter between text + reader. Implied reader.

concepts.name: postcolonial_criticism
concepts.definition: Said, Spivak, Bhabha. Literature in context of colonial + post-colonial power. Orientalism. Subaltern.

concepts.name: feminist_criticism
concepts.definition: Gilbert + Gubar, Showalter, Cixous, Kristeva. Patriarchy in literary tradition + canon; women's writing.

concepts.name: ecocriticism
concepts.definition: Literature + environment. Buell, Garrard. Nature in texts; literary response to ecological crisis.

concepts.name: canon_literary
concepts.definition: Set of works considered most important in tradition. Always contested. Expanded since 1970s.

concepts.name: intertextuality
concepts.definition: Kristeva. Every text in dialogue with prior texts. Echoes, allusions, parody.

concepts.name: genre_theory
concepts.definition: Texts classified by shared conventions. Generic expectations enable + constrain. Substrate analogue: substrate's pattern-matched response.

concepts.name: modernism
concepts.definition: Early 20th c. Formal experimentation; fragmented narrative; psychological depth. Joyce, Woolf, Eliot, Kafka.

concepts.name: postmodernism
concepts.definition: Mid-late 20th c. Metafiction, pastiche, distrust of grand narrative. Borges, Pynchon, DeLillo.

concepts.name: characterization
concepts.definition: How character is revealed: direct telling vs showing through action + speech. Round vs flat (Forster).

concepts.name: plot_aristotle
concepts.definition: Arrangement of events. Aristotle: beginning, middle, end with reversal + recognition. Freytag's pyramid: exposition, rising, climax, falling, resolution.

concepts.name: theme_literary
concepts.definition: Central idea or insight. Distinguishable from subject. Not stated baldly; emerges from work.

rules.name: meaning_emerges_from_form
rules.head: Jabberwock interprets a literary text
rules.body: form + content inseparable. New Criticism: how it's said constitutes what's said. Substrate's structure-as-meaning principle.

rules.name: intertextuality_situates_every_text
rules.head: Jabberwock reads a literary work
rules.body: the work converses with prior works through allusion, parody, echo. No text stands alone. Kristeva.

rules.name: irony_requires_double_register
rules.head: Jabberwock processes ironic statement
rules.body: literal meaning + intended meaning differ; competent reader holds both. Substrate's double-channel interpretation.

rules.name: narrator_reliability_must_be_assessed
rules.head: Jabberwock encounters first-person narration
rules.body: narrator's claims may diverge from what the text shows; reader infers reliability. Booth's unreliable narrator.

rules.name: reader_completes_text
rules.head: Jabberwock reads
rules.body: meaning emerges in encounter between text's gaps + reader's filling. Iser's implied reader. Substrate's reader-supplied content.
